parts: Lesson 8: Percentage and Its Applications — Summary

Percent means 'per hundred': 64% = 64/100 = 0.64. To change a percent to a fraction or decimal, drop % and divide by 100 (0.2% = 0.002); to change a fraction or decimal to a percent, multiply by 100 (16/25 = 64%, 3.7 = 370%, 0.025 = 2.5%). x% of a quantity = (x/100) × quantity. To find what percent A is of B, work out (A/B) × 100. Percentage increase or decrease = (change ÷ original value) × 100 — a fall from 150 to 100 is 50/150 × 100 = 33⅓%.
Successive changes multiply: +20% then −20% gives 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96, a net 4% decrease. If a price falls by r%, a fixed sum buys more; work with the money saved.

Cost price (C.P.) is what is paid, including overheads such as repairs and transport; selling price (S.P.) is what the article is sold for. Profit = S.P. − C.P.; loss = C.P. − S.P. Profit% = profit/C.P. × 100 and loss% = loss/C.P. × 100 — always on the C.P. S.P. = C.P. × (100 + gain%)/100 and S.P. = C.P. × (100 − loss%)/100. If C.P. = S.P. there is no profit and no loss.

Discount is a reduction on the marked (list) price: S.P. = M.P. − discount, and discount% = discount/M.P. × 100. A shopkeeper who marks goods 20% above cost and allows 10% discount sells at 1.2 × 0.9 = 1.08 of cost — a gain of 8%. Successive discounts are applied one after another, not added.
S.I. = P × R × T / 100, where P is the principal, R the rate per annum and T the time in years (6 months = ½ year). Amount = P + S.I. A sum doubles when S.I. = P, i.e. R × T = 100.

A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ, C.I. = A − P. When interest is compounded half-yearly, use R/2 per half-year and 2n periods: ₹12,000 at 4% for 1½ years half-yearly gives A = 12000 × (1.02)³ = ₹12,734.50. C.I. equals S.I. for the first period and is larger after that.

A value that grows at r% a year becomes V₀(1 + r/100)ⁿ; one that depreciates becomes V₀(1 − r/100)ⁿ. If the rate changes each year, multiply the year factors: a car worth ₹5,50,000 losing 15% in the first year and 10% in each later year is worth 550000 × 0.85 × 0.9 × 0.9 = ₹3,78,675 after 3 years. Population growth, business profit and loss, and machine depreciation are all worked this way.
